Task #24 phase 1 in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5, single H100: PROPAGATE the decoder lane's two kept hill-climb wins to the vit and mamba megakernel twins. HEAD≈276861d (decoder: H1 627d134 M-atom-interleaved fwd/dX wgmma + H3 a12c376 dW-tile interleave, both gated green; read BOTH diffs first — they are your exact templates).

THE TWO WINS TO PORT (mechanism: groups of kIL=2 consecutive m64 atoms issue back-to-back wgmmas into independent fp32 fragments sharing ONE staged operand tile -> tensor-pipe overlap + halved operand HBM traffic; ascending-k per atom preserved -> bit-exact):
1. H1: the forward/dX GEMM engine interleave (decoder's tc_gemm_block_unpipelined + DecTcSmem sA sizing).
2. H3: the dW tile path feeding MaxAtomsM>1 groups to that engine (decoder's dectc_dw_run_tile/_splitk drivers fed 2-atom groups; H3 notes it "ports verbatim").
TARGETS: csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_vit_tc.cuh + model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh (the decoder twins — find exact filenames; the vit/mamba TC stages mirror the decoder's structure) + their smem structs in fused_{vit,mamba}_megakernel.cuh. CHECK FIRST what's shared vs duplicated: if the GEMM engine is literally the same included helper, H1 may already be live for vit/mamba — then only the dW driver (H3) needs porting + verification. Measure, don't assume.

CONSTRAINTS/CAVEATS:
- vit: kSeq=17 quirks (its TILE_M macro is distinct, LCM-1088 constraint — do NOT touch tile sizes; only the atom-group interleave). mamba: 255 regs / occ-1 ZERO margin (the fit probe) — if the interleave pushes mamba past 255 regs -> occupancy 0 -> launcher refuses/GridBarrier hang; check ptxas regs after build; if it breaks the budget, try kIL=2 with reduced unroll or accept kIL=1 for mamba (document honestly).
- Even-atom-count assumption (H3 relied on decoder weights having even atom counts): VERIFY for vit/mamba weight shapes; handle odd counts with a tail group of 1 (no correctness shortcut).
- NO benchmark variant exists for vit/mamba (decoder_bench is decoder-only) — measure at PRODUCTION d=128 B=16384 via the same harness pattern: cheapest faithful = mirror tuning/decoder_bench.py into tuning/{vit,mamba}_bench.py only if quick, ELSE time via the roofline harness (python -m tuning.roofline --models vit,mamba) before/after. Production-scale improvement expected modest (decoder got -7.4% dW + -1.7% fwd at d=128) — ANY non-regression + the structural port landing green is the win here (the big payoff comes at ladder dims later).
GATES per model (never weaken): A/A/A bit-identical x3 on that model's cells AND wiring_check --require-all 33/33 AND tail-gates for that model (--cell adamw/vit + --cell supergrok2/vit for vit — SG2 exercises everything; --cell adamw/mamba + --cell prodigy/mamba for mamba) after production _ops rebuild AND the model's TC unit suite if one exists (find tests/hw/test_{vit,mamba}_tc.py or equivalent). Commit per green model ("vit TC: port M-atom interleave (H1+H3)..." then mamba). If a port fails irreconcilably (e.g. mamba reg budget), revert THAT model, keep the other, document.

DELIVERABLE: what was shared-vs-duplicated (did vit/mamba already inherit H1?); per-model before/after numbers (whatever harness you used, medians); ptxas reg/spill deltas for mamba; gate outputs raw; commit hashes; anything reverted+why. No report files.

commit 627d1340e143292e931909aaf54fbab2c3193a7b
Author: peterc04 <pcoy400@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 12 09:21:33 2026 +0000

    decoder TC: M-atom-interleaved wgmma GEMM pipeline (H1, task #13) — +22% @ d=1024, +1.7% @ d=128
    
    The L3-TC decoder GEMM microkernel (dectc::tc_gemm_block_unpipelined) ran each
    stacked m64 atom's K-chain to completion SEQUENTIALLY: every wgmma was followed
    by wait_group<0>, the shared B (weight) tile was re-staged ONCE PER ATOM, and the
    atom-a epilogue stores interleaved with atom-a+1's first wgmma (ptxas C7515, every
    build). The kernel is persistent one-CTA/SM (occupancy=1) so the wgmma latency +
    the redundant weight-operand HBM traffic were paid raw.
    
    FIX (shared dectc helper → lifts all decoder cells; vit/mamba twins later):
    process the m64 atoms in GROUPS of kIL = min(MaxAtomsM, SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_INTERLEAVE
    =2). Within a group each K-step issues the kIL wgmmas (one per atom) BACK-TO-BACK
    into INDEPENDENT fp32 fragments sharing ONE staged B-tile, before the single per-k
    wait. Two wins: (1) the kIL atoms have no accumulator RAW between them → the tensor
    pipe overlaps their MMA execution; (2) the B-tile (weights, HBM-bound) is staged
    once per group instead of per atom → kIL× less weight traffic. kIL capped at 2 so
    accumulator-reg + A-smem cost stays bounded (a dW tile can be 8 atoms). Production
    fwd/dX use kAtomsM=2 → full 2-wide interleave; dW uses MaxAtomsM=1 → kIL=1 (serial,
    unchanged). Per-atom accumulation stays ASCENDING-k (k=0 overwrite, k>0 add) →
    bitwise-identical numerics + A/A/A determinism. Ring smem A grows to
    kDecAtomsPerSlot(=2)·stages tiles (DecTcSmem 13.7→17.8KB; selftest arena + offsets
    follow).
    
    MEASURED (single H100, the committed decoder_bench loop):
      d=1024 B=16384:  2084.25 → 1624.74 ms/step   (-22.1%)
                       4.754  → 6.099 TF/s          (+28.3%, MFU 0.48% → 0.62%)
        per-phase (clock64): P1_fwd 525.6→301.9 ms (-42.6%), P1_bwd 571.7→328.6 ms
        (-42.5%) — the 2-atom fwd/dX GEMMs; P2_dW unchanged (433→438, kIL=1 by design).
      d=128  B=16384:  107.63 → 105.82 ms/step      (-1.7%, no production regression)
    
    GATES (all green):
      * d=1024 A/A/A: params+state+loss bit-identical across 3 runs.
      * wiring_check --require-all: 33/33 cells on L3-TC.
      * tail-gate adamw/decoder + muon/decoder (d=128, after _ops rebuild): PASS —
        state vs eager m≤2.2e-7/v≤9.6e-7 (adamw), 0/0 (muon); A/A/A bit-identical.
      * test_decoder_tc.py 18/18 (fwd/dX/dW × shapes incl. Nout=512→8-atom/4-group,
        dW determinism, full-cell oracle parity).
    
    NOTE: ptxas C7515 is still emitted (1×, 255 regs / 0 spills / 17844B smem at
    d=1024 — stack DROPPED 1152→640B). The win is the within-group MMA overlap + the
    B-staging-sharing, NOT C7515 removal: the CROSS-k accumulator chain (single fp32
    fragment, ascending-k) is inherently dependency-serialized, and true cross-k
    multi-in-flight needs the cp.async producer/consumer ring (a much larger rewrite,
    deferred). A single-fragment accumulator-lifetime restructure was tried first and
    REVERTED — it pushed the kernel to 255 regs + 5KB spills (worse), confirming the
    serialization is register/dependency-bound, not array-indexing-bound.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Excellent. The commit messages are very detailed. This is extremely informative. Key takeaways:

    the redundant weight-operand HBM traffic were paid raw.

    process the m64 atoms in GROUPS of kIL = min(MaxAtomsM, SG_TUNED_DEC_GEMM_INTERLEAVE
    =2). Within a group each K-step issues the kIL wgmmas (one per atom) BACK-TO-BACK
    into INDEPENDENT fp32 fragments sharing ONE staged B-tile, before the single per-k
    wait. Two wins: (1) the kIL atoms have no accumulator RAW between them → the tensor
    pipe overlaps their MMA execution; (2) the B-tile (weights, HBM-bound) is staged
    once per group instead of per atom → kIL× less weight traffic. kIL capped at 2 so
    accumulator-reg + A-smem cost stays bounded (a dW tile can be 8 atoms). Production
    fwd/dX use kAtomsM=2 → full 2-wide interleave; dW uses MaxAtomsM=1 → kIL=1 (serial,
    unchanged). Per-atom accumulation stays ASCENDING-k (k=0 overwrite, k>0 add) →

    follow).

This is the critical reality check. The mamba TC megakernel is **already at 255 registers** (the absolute ceiling for occupancy-1) with **2636 bytes of spills and 3408 bytes stack**. It is right at the edge. The task's caveat is real and severe: "mamba: 255 regs / occ-1 ZERO margin".

Since mamba's fwd/dX path uses `kAtomsM=1`, H1's interleave is a complete no-op for fwd/dX (kIL=1). The H1 engine change adds an `acc[kIL]` array where `kIL = min(MaxAtomsM, 2)`. For fwd/dX (MaxAtomsM=kAtomsM=1) → kIL=1 → `acc[1]` (same as a single accumulator, no register growth). For dW (H3 sets MaxAtomsM=2) → kIL=2 → `acc[2]` which adds N/2 = 64 fp32 registers worth of accumulator. 

The dW path is where mamba would gain (in_proj=8 atoms, dt_proj=4, out_proj=2). But adding a 2-wide accumulator to a kernel already at 255 regs with spills will likely push it further into spills or refuse to launch (occupancy 0). This is exactly the documented risk.

content.text:
The launcher refuses (returns error, no hang) if occupancy drops to 0. So if the mamba interleave pushes regs past what allows occupancy-1, the launcher will fail-closed (not hang) — which means the gates would catch it via a launch error, not a silent hang. That's somewhat safer than a hang, but still a failure.

Important strategic realization for mamba: 
- **fwd/dX H1 is a no-op** (kAtomsM=1 → kIL=1). Porting it changes the engine's structure (`acc[1]` instead of `acc[MaxAtomsM]` with the group loop) but for MaxAtomsM=1 it's functionally identical and shouldn't add registers. Actually it could even help since the current mamba engine uses `acc[MaxAtomsM]` which for dW=... wait, currently ALL mamba call sites use either `kAtomsM`(=1) or explicitly `MaxAtomsM=1`. So currently mamba's `acc[MaxAtomsM]` is always `acc[1]`. 
- The **only** register-increasing change for mamba is **H3** raising dW to `MaxAtomsM=kDwIL=2` → `acc[2]`. That's the risk.

So for mamba, the realistic plan:
1. Port H1 engine structure (interleave). With kIL=min(MaxAtomsM,2). For all current fwd/dX sites (MaxAtomsM=1) this is a no-op (kIL=1). **No register change.** This is safe and keeps the engine identical to decoder for maintainability.
2. Port H3 dW driver (MaxAtomsM=2). **This is the register risk.** Check ptxas after build. If it pushes occupancy to 0 / refuses → fall back to kIL=1 for mamba dW (document honestly).

- Mamba dW (H3) raises to MaxAtomsM=2 as well.

So mamba benefits from BOTH H1 and H3, but it's at 255 regs with 40B spill (adamw). The interleave adds an `acc[2]` array (vs current `acc[MaxAtomsM]=acc[2]` for fwd/dX already... wait, current mamba fwd/dX already passes `MaxAtomsM=kAtomsM=2`, so it ALREADY has `acc[2]`). 

So for mamba fwd/dX, the current engine already allocates `acc[2]` and runs them **serially** (atom 0 full k-chain, then atom 1). H1 changes this to run them **interleaved** (both atoms' wgmma per k-step into the 2 fragments). The register footprint of `acc[2]` is **unchanged** — both fragments are already live across the existing serial loop... 

Actually NO. In the current serial engine, `acc[a]` for a=0 is fully consumed (stored) before a=1's k-loop. But the array `acc[MaxAtomsM]` is declared with all MaxAtomsM fragments. With the decoder's pre-H1 code that's `acc[MaxAtomsM]` (all live across the atom loop). For mamba that's `acc[2]`. In H1, it becomes `acc[kIL]` = `acc[2]` (capped). **Same register count.** The interleave just changes the *issue order*, not the fragment count. For mamba dW: currently `MaxAtomsM=1` → `acc[1]`. H3 raises to `MaxAtomsM=kDwIL=2` → `acc[2]`. That's +1 fragment (64 fp32 regs for N=128... actually WgmmaAccum<128> has kRegs registers). THIS is the increase. Let me check WgmmaAccum register width.

"""tuning/vit_bench.py — production-scale ViT TC step benchmark (task #24 H1+H3 port).

Mirrors tuning/decoder_bench.py (there is no decoder-only bench variant for ViT;
the decoder_bench is decoder-only). JIT-compiles the SAME ViT TC cell TU
(csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_vit_real_adamw_tc.cu) as a SEPARATELY-NAMED coexisting
extension (own torch-extensions build dir + ninja incremental + sccache), so a
before/after knob sweep (-D SG_TUNED_VIT_GEMM_INTERLEAVE=1 vs default 2) rebuilds
incrementally and NEVER touches the production _ops.so or the 33/33 gate.

USAGE
  # Production d=128 (ViT D is fixed at 128) B=16384 median wall:
  python tuning/vit_bench.py --B 16384 --reps 5
  # Old serial GEMM (interleave width 1) for the before/after A/B:
  python tuning/vit_bench.py --B 16384 --reps 5 -D SG_TUNED_VIT_GEMM_INTERLEAVE=1

Notes:
  * ViT width is COMPILE-fixed (vit_layout kD=128); only B varies. Inputs are
    RANDOM (throughput, not a parity gate — correctness is the test suite's job).
  * Times the production tc_train_step at ncta_cap=0 (one CTA/SM, full saturation).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import statistics
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import torch  # noqa: E402
from torch.utils.cpp_extension import load  # noqa: E402

_TC_TU = str(ROOT / "csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_vit_real_adamw_tc.cu")


def build_variant(name: str | None = None, verbose: bool = False,
                  defines: list[str] | None = None):
    flags = ["-O3", "-std=c++17", "--expt-relaxed-constexpr",
             "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a",
             "-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=compute_90a"]
    suffix = ""
    if defines:
        for d_ in defines:
            flags.append("-D" + d_ if not d_.startswith("-D") else d_)
        norm = "_".join(d_.lstrip("-D").replace("=", "").replace(" ", "")
                        for d_ in defines)
        suffix = "_" + norm
    if name is None:
        name = "mega_vit_real_adamw_tc_bench" + suffix
    os.environ.setdefault("TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST", "9.0a")
    mod = load(name=name, sources=[_TC_TU],
               extra_include_paths=[str(ROOT)],
               extra_cuda_cflags=flags,
               extra_cflags=["-O3", "-std=c++17"],
               verbose=verbose)
    return mod


def measure(mod, B: int, reps: int, warmup: int, iters: int):
    from tests.hw.vit_oracle import NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, VOCAB
    dev = torch.device("cuda")
    total = int(mod.TOTAL)
    g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(42)
    params = (torch.randn(total, generator=g, device=dev) * 0.02).contiguous()
    patches = torch.randn(B, NUM_PATCHES, PATCH_DIM, generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.float32).contiguous()
    targets = torch.randint(0, VOCAB, (B,), generator=g, device=dev).to(torch.int32).contiguous()
    state = torch.zeros(3 * total, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    lr, beta1, beta2, eps, wd = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.98, 1e-8, 0.0
    bc1, bc2 = 1.0 - beta1, 1.0 - beta2

    def call():
        return mod.tc_train_step(params, patches, targets, state, lr, beta1, beta2,
                                 eps, wd, bc1, bc2, 1, 0)

    for _ in range(warmup):
        call()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()

    walls = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(iters):
            call()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) / iters)
    wall = statistics.median(walls)
    return {"B": B, "total_params": total, "wall_ms": wall * 1e3,
            "steps_per_s": 1.0 / wall, "walls_ms": [w * 1e3 for w in walls]}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--B", type=int, default=16384)
    ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=5)
    ap.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=20)
    ap.add_argument("--verbose-build", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("-D", dest="defines", action="append", default=[], metavar="KEY=VAL")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    assert args.B % 16 == 0, "B must be divisible by 16 (dW K-loop is 16-step atoms)"
    print(f"[vit-bench] building variant defines={args.defines}", flush=True)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    mod = build_variant(verbose=args.verbose_build, defines=args.defines)
    print(f"[vit-bench] build {time.perf_counter()-t0:.1f}s  TILE_M={int(mod.TILE_M)} "
          f"TOTAL={int(mod.TOTAL):,} TILE_N={int(mod.TILE_N)}", flush=True)
    res = measure(mod, args.B, args.reps, args.warmup, args.iters)
    print(f"\n[vit-bench] B={res['B']}  params={res['total_params']:,}", flush=True)
    print(f"  wall/step = {res['wall_ms']:.4f} ms  "
          f"(median of {[f'{x:.3f}' for x in res['walls_ms']]})", flush=True)
    print(f"  steps/s   = {res['steps_per_s']:.4f}", flush=True)
    return res


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The critical question: does it still achieve occupancy-1 (the launcher's refuse check)? But I used `smemA + ((int64_t)s * kMbAtomsPerSlot + ai) * kMbTcSmemA1` — I used `kMbAtomsPerSlot` (the smem-allocation width) as the stride multiplier, while the decoder used `kIL` (the interleave group width).

## Task #24 Phase 1 — COMPLETE

Both decoder hill-climb wins (H1 forward/dX GEMM interleave + H3 dW tile interleave) ported to the **vit** and **mamba** megakernel twins. Both landed green and committed.

### Shared-vs-duplicated (the first thing the task asked to measure, not assume)
The GEMM engine is **DUPLICATED, not shared** — neither twin inherited H1. Each model has its own `tc_gemm_block_unpipelined` in its own namespace (`vittc::`, `mbtc::`), and neither references `dectc::`. So H1 was **not** already live for either; both the engine (H1) and the dW driver (H3) had to be ported per-model. Critically, the two twins had **diverged differently** from the decoder:
- **mamba** kept the decoder's exact structure (S-stage ring + `stage_k`/`issue_k` lambdas + `acc[MaxAtomsM]`) → near-verbatim port (`dectc`→`mbtc` renames).
- **vit** had been rewritten to a **single reused accumulator with no ring** — because vit's `kAtomsM=17` made `acc[17]` spill to local memory (C7515). So vit was a port to a structurally *different* (unpipelined) engine, not a copy.

### Per-model before/after (single H100, production B=16384, median of 5; new `tuning/{vit,mamba}_bench.py` mirroring `decoder_bench.py`)
| Model | HEAD baseline | H1+H3 | Δ | serial-refactor (interleave=1) A/B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **vit** | 166.59 ms | **123.58 ms** | **−25.8%** | 146.43 ms (interleave itself −15.6%) |
| **mamba** | 108.03 ms | **102.70 ms** | **−4.9%** | 105.65 ms (interleave itself −2.8%) |

vit far exceeded the expected "modest" gain because the interleave **eliminated the engine's register spills** (see below) on top of the MMA-overlap/operand-sharing win. (mamba's TILE_M=128→kAtomsM=2, so its fwd/dX *do* interleave — not the no-op I first suspected before checking.)

### ptxas reg/spill deltas (`fused_*_megakernel_tc`, OptId 0 = AdamW)
| | vit baseline | vit after | mamba baseline | mamba after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registers | 255 | 255 | 255 | **255 (held)** |
| Spill stores | **6452 B** | **0 B** | 40 B | 40 B |
| Spill loads | 6676 B | 0 B | 108 B | 96 B |
| Stack | 2704 B | 672 B | 1424 B | 2224 B |
| smem | 7664 B | 9712 B | 14800 B | 18896 B |

**Mamba's 255-reg/occ-1 zero-margin caveat held** — kIL=2, occupancy-1 preserved (the GridBarrier launcher did not refuse), spills unchanged, **no fallback to kIL=1 needed**. The register-pressure-sensitive prodigy/mamba and supergrok2/mamba cells still pass A/A/A. Even-atom assumption: verified per-weight; mamba's **x_proj (Nout=40 → 1 atom, ODD)** is handled by the ragged-tail logic (the one weight the decoder's all-even shortcut would have broken) — it cost one extra 64×N split-K slot, documented in-source. vit weights are all even.

**Nothing reverted.** Both ports kept.

The one honest caveat: **`test_mamba_tc.py` is 3-fail/2-pass — but PRE-EXISTING at HEAD, not a regression.** I verified by checking out HEAD's mamba headers, rebuilding, and rerunning: `test_tc_single_step_grad_parity`, `test_tc_proj_dw_exact_on_own_operands`, and `test_tc_determinism` **already fail on unmodified 276861d**.
